title: Presentism as an Empirical Hypothesis
relevance: Primary source of the law-constitutive unity criterion and of the ground-vs-complete-description contrast this task tests (ss. 6-8).
limits: Complete public copy downloaded this run; SHA-256 c93ca072e14c4fd0f1c638ff960db17847231479ec9bf168cf0d69f9644bb054, matching paper/SOURCE_AUDIT.md and paper/reviews/savitt-delta/REVIEW.md. Text extracted via PDFKit; load-bearing passages read in context (ss. 6-8); remaining sections extraction-scanned only. Published-layout copy not collated against the publisher version. Journal pagination (p. 1109 disjunction sentence; p. 1110 subsystems passage) inherited from the project's hash-verified audits, confirmed by verbatim match with Savitt's cited locator.
exact_version_doi: Philosophy of Science 80(5): 1101-1111, December 2013 (publisher metadata via CUP abstract page, vol/pages matching); no DOI printed on the inspected copy
section_locator: s. 6 p. 1109: 'the spatiotemporal extent of the sufficient dynamical ground of a given unity might turn out to be much, much smaller than the abstract spatiotemporal structure within which the evolution of that unity is completely described, or it might be the size of the block universe. This is an empirical matter...'; s. 7 p. 1109: 'The present is a spatiotemporal region of whatever size is necessary to sustain the dynamical system in question.' with fn. 7 ('All the ontology is carried by the dynamics...'); s. 8 p. 1110: 'let us begin from the position that there are genuine subsystems... The ground of what is real is the dynamics'
assumptions: Unity of things grounded in dynamical laws (Newton as read via DiSalle); spacetime assigned epistemic, not ontological, role; P1/P2 clash with SR treated as shared-assumption artifact
conclusion: A dynamics-relative present: for each thing, a region 'of whatever size is necessary to sustain the dynamical system in question'; its extent is an open empirical matter, possibly as large as the block universe, in which case the presentism proposed is defeated
proof_status: Philosophical program, not a theorem; the author marks the empirical question open; no subsystem criterion, measurement protocol, or likelihood model is given (confirmed by the project's primary-review lane and by this run's reading)
open_questions: Does any dynamical criterion in physical quantities discriminate 'sufficient dynamical ground' from 'complete description' within Markovian Newtonian systems? (Our RESULT.md s. 4: no, up to premise P.)
Newton scholarship via DiSalle not independently audited here

title: Virtual potentials for feedback traps
relevance: Laboratory anchor for the delayed-coupling boundary system: a real bound-particle system whose confinement has physically integral delay and update times, so no instantaneous description is the trapping fact.
limits: Author-hosted PRE PDF fetched via exa; abstract and s. I (introduction) read; body, methods, and simulations not read this run. Abstract-level claims only are used: finite time scales (delay, update time, exposure) and the sampling-time bound on trappable size.
exact_version_doi: Physical Review E 86, 061106 (2012); DOI 10.1103/PhysRevE.86.061106; received 15 Sep 2012, published 5 Dec 2012
section_locator: Abstract; s. I Introduction (ABEL trap, feedback protocol F_n = -dU/dx at estimated position, sampling period t_s)
assumptions: Markovian idealization fails at finite sampling: dynamics modeled with timing effects of the loop
conclusion: For small feedback gains the motion approximates a particle in an ordinary harmonic potential; approximation quality set by the ratio of loop update time to the virtual-potential relaxation time
proof_status: Peer-reviewed experimental/theoretical paper; its internal proofs not audited (not read at that depth)
open_questions: Whether the delay differential model used in RESULT.md s. 3.3 faithfully matches the sampled-hold loop structure (engineered-loop idealization flagged as a limitation)
